text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband, Asif Ali Zardari, has been detained at the Sihala Rest House near Islamabad under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, the Lahore High Court was informed.
- Mumtaz Ali Bhutto, estranged uncle of Benazir Bhutto, was sworn in as caretaker chief minister of the Sindh Province.

- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has indicated that some politicians may be barred from contesting the elections, set for February 3, by disqualifying them through an accountability law likely to be enacted in the next few days.
- Officials at the Finance Ministry have refused to comment on downgrading of Pakistan's credit rating to B2 from B1 by the New York-based credit rating agency Moody's.
- Bhutto will file a petition in the Supreme Court next week against her government's dismissal by the president.
- Stocks declined sharply followed by heavy selling after Moody's downgraded Pakistan's credit rating.
- Pakistan Muslim League party president Nawaz Sharif said a permanent accountability commission should be set up that should continue after the elections.
- The International Monetary Fund is discussing a stalled standby loan with Pakistan and will make a decision in the next few days, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said.
- The government has suspended 19 ambassadors who had been appointed by the ousted government of Benazir Bhutto from outside the professional diplomatic service.
- A reshuffle, initiated with the dismissal of the PPP government, continued as more than 24 top bureaucrats were transferred and several officials on contract were sacked.
- Pakistan has called upon India to remove all kinds of restrictions, export subsidies and hidden concessions in order to open formal trade between the two countries.
- Meraj Khalid arrived in Lahore, the Punjab province capital, travelling economy class on a Pakistan International Airlines flight and used the ordinary lounge.
- Two bombs rocked government offices at Nawabshah town of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's home province of Sindh but only a visiting villager was slightly injured.
- The Election Commission of Pakistan will meet on November 11 to discuss arrangements for holding elections on February 3.
